method_vectors.scope: Actual WindowsIntel/WindowsIntelPAE/WindowsIntel32e read with physical and explicit swap BufferDataLayers over synthetic page tables. Resident/transition/prototype flags, fixed swap bits and indices, unaligned/cross-page reads, upper-level software entries, missing attachments, backing and table holes are covered. Synthetic adapters do not establish all scanner mapping/chunk/padding or full architecture/platform/exception/resource contracts. Reference swap reads intentionally preserve the pinned offset semantics.

mcp_regression.scope: Eight analyses in one persistent isolated MCP session, including PID lists/union, maxsize and repeat. Every immutable result page is fetched and all rows compared in order with no-cache native output, preserving partial state and pinned layer policy. No success cache files are created for partial captures. Native API regression, not additional reference differential evidence.

limitations: The canonical Windows VadRegExScan input and display readers now use pinned Windows Intel resident/transition and explicit swap rules; native prototype/compressed recovery remains available in the general reader and other native consumers. This is not proof that every plugin uses the reference layer policy.
All byte vectors compare successful read bytes or failure, not exact exception types/messages. Synthetic x86/PAE/x64 reads are not a complete platform/discovery contract.

Reference swap base/unaligned-offset and large PAT semantics are intentionally preserved; native ISF software-page recovery remains a separate policy. Partial/empty regular attachments are accepted with per-read bounds and mutation validation.
ARM64 retains native recovery because the pinned reference lacks a Windows ARM64 layer; no ARM64 parity is claimed.

Real rows use one public Win10 sample and one shared frozen PDB-derived ISF. Layer scanning/padding/chunks, arbitrary Python/PCRE2 patterns, live races and all fault/resource contracts remain incompletely validated.
Capture holes and damaged VAD/process-tree diagnostics remain partial; field and sequence agreement is not evidence of complete capture. No complete plugin contract is claimed.
